items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: And Gene Montooth comes up to me and he at the time had a goatee and he was what we would call a hippie.

ctx.x: Yeah. I’m glad you asked me that because I have, the lady that helped me get this started, her — I think her address is over on my thing and I almost wrote her a letter. I’ve been waiting since — I’ve been waiting over 60 years to write her a letter. When I was in college I told everybody I wouldn’t be a teacher because some of the students that I heard practicing in the rooms next to me and the recitals that I had to go to, I didn’t think they played their instrument very well. So back then I was very naïve. I…

a teacher you had to really play well, because you’re going to be an example. So I told everybody I wouldn’t be a teacher. But yet when I got up to about my fourth year, senior year, I was out in the parking lot, it might have been my junior year in the spring. And Gene Montooth comes up to me and he at the time had a goatee and he was what we would call a hippie. Played tenor, okay? Played oboe, maybe bassoon I can’t remember. But he came up and said, “Hey Jamey, I’ve got a job teaching in the fall, high school.…

Terrific story. And I wanted to speak about “So What” actually but a little later. Now we’ve got two laters. So this developed into this idea of recording a piano trio and assembling what you felt was enough information to get people started. Did you have trouble in a couple of things. First of all do you recall if the piano trio had to do some adjusting because they weren’t backing anybody up? They were just playing. Was that difficult for them at first?
